thread:
maria-cs: Heads-up — Argus onboarding run hitting intermittent 403s immediately followed by 429 spikes after they switched to a per-job runner.

maria-cs: Quick summary: ephemeral tokens (TTL=45s) + per-job local cache + many short-lived worker processes. We see auth OK then 403 then a flood of retries that flip into 429s.

maria-cs: relevant log snippet:
```
200 OK -> 403 Forbidden -> 429 Rate Limit within ~3s
Auth: Bearer <redacted>
X-Req-ID: req_0a1b2c
```

abby-qa: I wrote a tiny Node repro — runner spawns 40 workers, each keeps token for 45s but refreshes non-atomically. At t=45s we get a refresh storm.

abby-qa: minimal sketch:
```
workers = spawn(40)
workers.forEach(w => w.cacheToken(ttl=45))
// no lock -> many refreshes simultaneously
```

chris-se: Two likely causes: (1) TTL too short for per-job lifetime and (2) concurrent refresh fanout + naive retry/backoff. Also saw a few requests missing x-client-id — their forked worker strips extra headers.

chris-se: checklist for Argus:
- bump token TTL for now
- add refresh-lock (single inflight refresh per process)
- add randomized jitter to refresh timing
- ensure x-client-id present so we can correlate concurrency
- check client clock / NTP

kevin-infra: Ops can allow a temporary onboarding exemption to the per-minute handshake limits for named accounts. I can open a 2-hour soft window with audit logs.

kevin-infra: short-term mitigation options:
1) increase ephemeral TTL to 5m for their env (temp)
2) enable soft burst allowance for their org for 2h

chris-se: SDK quick patch we can share:
```js
// single-refresh promise lock
if (!token || token.expired()) {
  if (!refreshInFlight) refreshInFlight = doRefresh().finally(()=> refreshInFlight = null)
  await refreshInFlight
}
```

abby-qa: Adding exponential backoff + jitter to retries removed the 429 waterfall in my local runs.

maria-cs: Argus contact (sam_argus) ok with TTL bump for demo tomorrow but wants an example they can drop-in today. They will also try to preserve x-client-id in their fork.

onboard-bot: ticket created ORG-9901 "Argus onboarding - ephemeral token refresh storm" assigned chris-se, kevin-infra. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ORG-9901

maria-cs: test plan in the ticket: reduce workers -> 10, TTL=300s, enable jitter, run 2000 requests over 5 mins. Goal: no auth-flap and <1% 429s.

chris-se: If they still see issues after TTL bump, ask for traces with x-client-id and a sample of request headers and server times. We'll also check server-side per-minute handshake counts and clock skew.

sam_argus: Thanks — implementing TTL=5m + header fix now. Will ping after 10:30am PT dry-run. Appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:
